title: Ada the Attendant
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In the Jerusalem Talmud, end of Terumot, and Shabbat 2:1: Ada the attendant asked Rabbi Ami, “Since I dip a wick [in ordinary oil; supplied מן חולה]…?” He said to him: “It is nullified on the wicks.” Penei Moshe explains that he asked about impure terumah oil designated for burning, which Hyman considers consistent with the context; Korban HaEdah explains that he attended the sick.
Hyman reports that some wish to say that he is Ada Dayyala, but Ada Dayyala was in Babylonia and this one was in the Land of Israel.

notes.text: Saved Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:1 explains dipping one wick in ordinary oil, among wicks soaked in impure terumah oil; the ordinary oil is nullified among the others. The source’s מן חולה is not translated as taking a wick from an ill person. Korban HaEdah’s different sick-attendant interpretation remains explicitly attributed, and Hyman’s rejection of the Babylonian Ada Dayyala identity stays distinct.
